svg.text: 12 nodes · 16 relationships · 11 implied labels, generated from the official MITRE ATT&CK 20.1 STIX bundles of the Enterprise, Mobile and ICS domains. The main arrows are named by their relationship type; hover any arrow for its name and description, and cards link to the object's page on attack.mitre.org.
Adversary — groups, campaigns, malware and tools
Defence — mitigations, detection strategies, analytics and data components
Foundation — the ATTACKObject label and ICS assets
STIX relationship object: source to target
embedded reference: kill chain phases, analytic references or log source references
subtype: also carries the supertype's label

path.title: LOG_SOURCE_REF: A data component the log sources of an analytic collect, from its `x_mitre_log_source_references`. Links 5233 pairs in MITRE ATT&CK 20.1: Enterprise 4190, Mobile 614, ICS 429. e.g. Analytic 0001 (AN0001) watches the data component Cloud Service Metadata (DC0070); Analytic 0002 (AN0002) watches the data component Network Connection Creation (DC0082); Analytic 0003 (AN0003) watches the data component Process Creation (DC0032).

ATTRIBUTED_TO: The campaign is attributed to the group it is attributed to. Links 27 pairs in MITRE ATT&CK 20.1: Enterprise 26, ICS 5, Mobile 1. e.g. C0011 is attributed to Transparent Tribe; C0017 is attributed to APT41; Operation Dream Job is attributed to Lazarus Group.

USES: The source uses the target in the course of an attack: a group or campaign uses a technique, malware or tool; malware or a tool uses a technique. Links 96 pairs in MITRE ATT&CK 20.1: Enterprise 92, ICS 6, Mobile 3. e.g. Night Dragon uses ASPXSpy; CostaRicto uses PS1; Operation Spalax uses njRAT.

USES: The source uses the target in the course of an attack: a group or campaign uses a technique, malware or tool; malware or a tool uses a technique. Links 1351 pairs in MITRE ATT&CK 20.1: Enterprise 1213, Mobile 44, ICS 94. e.g. Frankenstein uses Data from Local System; Night Dragon uses Security Account Manager; CostaRicto uses Data from Local System.

USES: The source uses the target in the course of an attack: a group or campaign uses a technique, malware or tool; malware or a tool uses a technique. Links 81 pairs in MITRE ATT&CK 20.1: Enterprise 81. e.g. Frankenstein uses Empire; Night Dragon uses gsecdump; CostaRicto uses PsExec.

ANALYTIC_REF: The analyses a detection strategy holds, from its `x_mitre_analytic_refs`. Links 2271 pairs in MITRE ATT&CK 20.1: Enterprise 1758, Mobile 213, ICS 300. e.g. Detect Access to Cloud Instance Metadata API (IaaS) has Analytic 0001 (AN0001); Behavioral Detection of Publish/Subscribe Protocol Misuse for C2 has Analytic 0002 (AN0002); T1136.002 Detection Strategy - Domain Account Creation Across Platforms has Analytic 0006 (AN0006).

DETECTS: The detection strategy detects the technique it detects. Links 935 pairs in MITRE ATT&CK 20.1: Enterprise 706, Mobile 125, ICS 104. e.g. Detect Access to Cloud Instance Metadata API (IaaS) detects Cloud Instance Metadata API; Behavioral Detection of Publish/Subscribe Protocol Misuse for C2 detects Publish/Subscribe Protocols; T1136.002 Detection Strategy - Domain Account Creation Across Platforms detects Domain Account.

USES: The source uses the target in the course of an attack: a group or campaign uses a technique, malware or tool; malware or a tool uses a technique. Links 705 pairs in MITRE ATT&CK 20.1: Enterprise 691, Mobile 17, ICS 16. e.g. Axiom uses Hikit; Moafee uses PoisonIvy; Cleaver uses TinyZBot.

USES: The source uses the target in the course of an attack: a group or campaign uses a technique, malware or tool; malware or a tool uses a technique. Links 4889 pairs in MITRE ATT&CK 20.1: Enterprise 4815, Mobile 35, ICS 39. e.g. Axiom uses Steganography; Moafee uses Binary Padding; Cleaver uses LSASS Memory.

USES: The source uses the target in the course of an attack: a group or campaign uses a technique, malware or tool; malware or a tool uses a technique. Links 475 pairs in MITRE ATT&CK 20.1: Enterprise 475. e.g. Cleaver uses Mimikatz; Ke3chang uses Mimikatz; APT12 uses HTRAN.

USES: The source uses the target in the course of an attack: a group or campaign uses a technique, malware or tool; malware or a tool uses a technique. Links 12351 pairs in MITRE ATT&CK 20.1: Enterprise 10739, Mobile 1438, ICS 174. e.g. Trojan.Mebromi uses System Firmware; RIPTIDE uses Web Protocols; TinyZBot uses Keylogging.

MITIGATES: The mitigation prevents, or makes harder, the technique it mitigates. Links 2068 pairs in MITRE ATT&CK 20.1: Enterprise 1477, Mobile 167, ICS 424. e.g. Authorization Enforcement mitigates Activate Firmware Update Mode; Access Management mitigates Activate Firmware Update Mode; Communication Authenticity mitigates Activate Firmware Update Mode.

KILL_CHAIN_PHASE: The tactic a technique serves, from the `kill_chain_phases` of the technique. Links 1149 pairs in MITRE ATT&CK 20.1: Enterprise 881, Mobile 145, ICS 123. e.g. Activate Firmware Update Mode serves the Inhibit Response Function tactic; Monitor Process State serves the Collection tactic; Automated Collection serves the Collection tactic.

SUBTECHNIQUE_OF: The technique is a sub-technique of the more general technique it is of. Links 552 pairs in MITRE ATT&CK 20.1: Enterprise 479, Mobile 47, ICS 26. e.g. Download All is a sub-technique of Program Download; Online Edit is a sub-technique of Program Download; Program Append is a sub-technique of Program Download.

TARGETS: The technique targets the asset it targets. Links 933 pairs in MITRE ATT&CK 20.1: ICS 933. e.g. Activate Firmware Update Mode targets Human-Machine Interface (HMI); Monitor Process State targets Human-Machine Interface (HMI); Automated Collection targets Programmable Logic Controller (PLC).

USES: The source uses the target in the course of an attack: a group or campaign uses a technique, malware or tool; malware or a tool uses a technique. Links 891 pairs in MITRE ATT&CK 20.1: Enterprise 869, Mobile 22. e.g. Mimikatz uses LSASS Memory; Windows Credential Editor uses LSASS Memory; pwdump uses Security Account Manager.
Every Tactic is also a ATTACKObject
Every Technique is also a ATTACKObject
Every Campaign is also a ATTACKObject
Every Group is also a ATTACKObject
Every Malware is also a ATTACKObject

Every Analytic is also a ATTACKObject
Every DataComponent is also a ATTACKObject
Every DetectionStrategy is also a ATTACKObject
Every Mitigation is also a ATTACKObject
Every Asset is also a ATTACKObject

g.title: ATTACKObject — An object of the MITRE ATT&CK knowledge base: a tactic, technique, mitigation, group, campaign, malware, tool, detection strategy, analytic, data component or asset. Every node carries this label, 5657 in MITRE ATT&CK 20.1; the label of its category, e.g. Technique, says what kind of object it is. Properties: stixId, name, description, url, created, modified, domains, version

Tactic — A tactic: the 'why' of an attack, the adversary's tactical objective, e.g. Stealth or Privilege Escalation. Techniques serve a tactic through the technique's kill chain phases. Holds 39 Tactic objects in MITRE ATT&CK 20.1: Enterprise 15, Mobile 12, ICS 12. Examples: Initial Access, Execution, Persistence. Properties: stixId, attackId, shortname

Technique — A technique: the 'how' of an attack, the means by which an adversary achieves a tactical objective. A sub-technique is a more specific technique, linked to its parent by SUBTECHNIQUE_OF. Holds 935 Technique objects in MITRE ATT&CK 20.1: Enterprise 706, Mobile 125, ICS 104. Examples: Activate Firmware Update Mode, Monitor Process State, Automated Collection. Properties: stixId, attackId, platforms, isSubtechnique, impactType, remoteSupport, tacticType

Campaign — A campaign: a grouping of intrusion activity conducted over a specific period of time against specific targets. Holds 61 Campaign objects in MITRE ATT&CK 20.1: Enterprise 57, Mobile 3, ICS 10. Examples: Frankenstein, Night Dragon, CostaRicto. Properties: stixId, attackId, aliases, firstSeen, lastSeen

Group — A group: a set of related intrusion activity that ATT&CK tracks by a common name, e.g. an APT or a criminal organisation. Holds 182 Group objects in MITRE ATT&CK 20.1: Enterprise 178, Mobile 20, ICS 14. Examples: Axiom, Moafee, Cleaver. Properties: stixId, attackId, aliases

Malware — Malware: a piece of software an adversary uses to compromise a system, e.g. a backdoor, ransomware or an implant. Holds 875 Malware objects in MITRE ATT&CK 20.1: Enterprise 747, Mobile 127, ICS 25. Examples: Trojan.Mebromi, RIPTIDE, TinyZBot. Properties: stixId, attackId, aliases, platforms, isFamily

Tool — A tool: a legitimate piece of software an adversary uses, e.g. a command-line utility, a remote access tool or a credential dumper. Holds 97 Tool objects in MITRE ATT&CK 20.1: Enterprise 95, Mobile 2. Examples: Mimikatz, Windows Credential Editor, pwdump. Properties: stixId, attackId, aliases, platforms

Analytic — An analytic: the logic of a detection, such as a sensor and the condition it watches for, with the data components its log sources collect. Holds 2286 Analytic objects in MITRE ATT&CK 20.1: Enterprise 1773, Mobile 213, ICS 300. Examples: Analytic 0001, Analytic 0002, Analytic 0003. Properties: stixId, attackId, platforms

DataComponent — A data component: a conceptual piece of data that an analytic's log sources collect, e.g. Process Creation or Network Connection Creation. Holds 120 DataComponent objects in MITRE ATT&CK 20.1: Enterprise 106, Mobile 29, ICS 40. Examples: Scheduled Job Creation, User Account Authentication, Malware Metadata. Properties: stixId, attackId

DetectionStrategy — A detection strategy: one approach to detecting a technique, holding the analytics that implement it. Holds 935 DetectionStrategy objects in MITRE ATT&CK 20.1: Enterprise 706, Mobile 125, ICS 104. Examples: Detect Access to Cloud Instance Metadata API (IaaS), Behavioral Detection of Publish/Subscribe Protocol Misuse for C2, T1136.002 Detection Strategy - Domain Account Creation Across Platforms. Properties: stixId, attackId

Mitigation — A mitigation: a security control that prevents a technique, or makes it harder, e.g. Multi-factor Authentication or Network Segmentation. Holds 109 Mitigation objects in MITRE ATT&CK 20.1: Enterprise 44, Mobile 13, ICS 53. Examples: Authorization Enforcement, Access Management, Communication Authenticity. Properties: stixId, attackId

Asset — An asset: a kind of ICS system or device that a technique targets, e.g. a control server or a field controller. Holds 18 Asset objects in MITRE ATT&CK 20.1: ICS 18. Examples: Workstation, Human-Machine Interface (HMI), Programmable Logic Controller (PLC). Properties: stixId, attackId, sectors, platforms
